Design-based structural equation models.

Source: R/generics.R
svysem.Rd

svysem(), svycfa() and svygrowth() fit a lavaan model to a survey::svydesign() object. Sampling weights, strata and primary sampling units enter the standard errors through the design-based covariance of the sample moments (Gamma), which is passed to lavaan as NACOV together with the raw data and the sampling weights. The fit is not built from sample moments. svysem() uses the defaults of lavaan::sem(), svycfa() those of lavaan::cfa(), and svygrowth() those of lavaan::growth(). Arguments in ... are passed on to that fitter.

svysem(
  model,
  design,
  estimator = c("MLM", "WLSMV", "MLR"),
  replicates = NULL,
  replicate.type = NULL,
  parallel = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

Model syntax, as for lavaan::sem(), lavaan::cfa() or lavaan::growth().

design

A survey.design, survey.design2, or svyrep.design object, including the result of subset() or survey::as.svrepdesign().

estimator

Variance estimator. "MLM" (Satorra-Bentler for one group, replicate weights when group= is set; complete continuous data), "WLSMV" (ordinal weighted least squares with replicate-weight standard errors), or "MLR" (Yuan-Bentler, including missing = "ml").

replicates

Number of bootstrap replicate weights. Used when replicate.type = "bootstrap" for WLSMV or for MLM with group=. Jackknife and BRR counts are fixed by the primary sampling units.

replicate.type

How survey::as.svrepdesign() builds weights for WLSMV and for MLM with group=. One of "auto", "JK1", "JKn", "BRR", or "bootstrap". NULL is "auto".

parallel

NULL, or a function of (X, FUN) with the same contract as lapply(), used to loop WLSMV replicates and multigroup MLM replicates. On a svyimputationList, parallel loops imputations instead, and the replicates inside each imputation stay sequential.

...

Passed to lavaan::sem(), lavaan::cfa() or lavaan::growth(). data, sampling.weights, sample moments, NACOV, and WLS.V are taken from the design. ov.order is set internally so Gamma matches the model.

Value

An S4 object of class svysem that contains the lavaan fit. Slots are df (design degrees of freedom), estimator ("MLM", "WLSMV", or "MLR"), variance_method ("linearization" or "replication") and svysem_call.

Details

The returned object extends lavaan, so coef(), vcov(), lavaan::lavTestWald() and lavaan::fitMeasures() report design-based results. parameterEstimates() and standardizedSolution() include the design-based standard errors and confidence intervals. lavaan's own functions omit those columns unless se = TRUE, because the object's class is svysem rather than lavaan. summary() and the printed display add the design degrees of freedom and the estimator.

"MLM" is maximum likelihood with a Satorra-Bentler adjustment for complete continuous data. missing = "ml" is an error and names MLR as the estimator that handles it. Rows that are incomplete on the model variables are not dropped: their sampling weight is set to 0 inside the design used for Gamma, which is how subset() represents a domain, and the primary sampling unit structure is kept. Zero weights are legal. A negative weight, or a design with no positive weight, is an error.

lavaan's default sampling.weights.normalization = "total" rescales weights so that they sum to the number of rows. Means and covariances of products are invariant to that constant, so Gamma is computed from the design's sampling weights on the same rows. The products use the maximum likelihood divisor (the weighted residual products, with no n / (n - 1) factor). survey::svyvar() is not used. Means and second-moment products are stacked in one linearization, so the covariance between them is kept; that term is what makes a regression intercept match survey::svyglm().

Gamma follows lavaan's model order (ov.order = "force.model" on the fit that receives NACOV). Without that argument lavaan reorders variables to the data order and pairs Gamma with the wrong columns. fixed.x = TRUE, the default for lavaan::sem(), is supported when those columns are the observed second moments, plus the means when a mean structure is estimated. conditional.x = TRUE is not supported for MLM or MLR. MLR fits one group of continuous variables. Single-group MLM does too, by linearization. group= on MLM refits the weighted model on replicate weights, because lavaan keeps one NACOV per group and that drops the covariance between groups. The multigroup chi-square is the maximum-likelihood statistic, not a Satorra-Bentler statistic. Clustering is taken from the design; do not pass cluster=, which would double-count primary sampling units. survey.lonely.psu is read by survey::svymean() and is never set here.

"MLR" is robust maximum likelihood with a Yuan-Bentler adjustment. The variance is a sandwich: lavaan's observed information, and a meat from the design variance of the casewise scores (survey::svytotal()). missing = "ml" scores the observed indicators; it does not fall back to complete cases. On a survey.design the variance method is linearization. On a svyrep.design it is replication, because survey::svytotal() uses the replicate weights.

"WLSMV" is lavaan's weighted least squares with the diagonally weighted least squares matrix taken from the weighted sample. Point estimates match that weighted fit. Standard errors and the scaled test use the replicate-weight covariance of lavaan's sample statistics (thresholds, continuous means and variances, and correlations), with the scale from survey::as.svrepdesign() and survey::svrVar(). replicate.type = "auto" is a stratified jackknife when the design has strata and JK1 otherwise. replicates is only the bootstrap count. Ordered indicators, group=, and missing = "pairwise" or "listwise" are accepted. lavaan stores one NACOV per group, so the covariance of sample statistics between groups is not passed on. The weight matrix Mplus uses for TYPE = COMPLEX has not been compared with lavaan's. For WLSMV, MLR, and multigroup MLM, se and test are set by the design and are not taken from ....

A svyrep.design is accepted for every estimator. variance_method is then "replication". replicates and replicate.type are an error on a design that already has replicate weights.

predict() returns factor scores for continuous outcomes. See predict.svysem().

References

Oberski D (2014). "lavaan.survey: An R Package for Complex Survey Analysis of Structural Equation Models." Journal of Statistical Software, 57(1), 1–27. doi:10.18637/jss.v057.i01

Yuan KH, Bentler PM (2000). "Three Likelihood-Based Methods for Mean and Covariance Structure Analysis with Nonnormal Missing Data." Sociological Methodology, 30(1), 165–200. doi:10.1111/0081-1750.00078

See also

svysem, predict.svysem(), simulate_design(), lavaan::sem(), survey::svydesign(), survey::svyglm()

Examples

design <- simulate_design(n_psu = 6, n_per = 4, n_strata = 2, seed = 1)
fit <- svysem(
  "y ~ x1 + x2", design,
  fixed.x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE
)
fit
#> svysem fit
#> Estimator: MLM
#> Variance method: linearization
#> Design df: 10
#> lavaan 0.7-3 ended normally after 1 iteration
#> 
#>   Estimator                                         ML
#>   Optimization method                           NLMINB
#>   Number of model parameters                         9
#> 
#>   Number of observations                                  48
#>   Sampling weights variable                   .svysem_weight
#> 
#> Model Test User Model:
#>                                               Standard      Scaled
#>   Test Statistic                                 0.000       0.000
#>   Degrees of freedom                                 0           0
coef(fit)
#>   y~x1   y~x2   y~~y x1~~x1 x1~~x2 x2~~x2    y~1   x1~1   x2~1 
#>  0.441 -0.483  0.880  0.726 -0.085  0.958  0.902  0.088  0.104 
vcov(fit)
#>          y~x1   y~x2   y~~y x1~~x1 x1~~x2 x2~~x2    y~1   x1~1   x2~1
#> y~x1    0.048                                                        
#> y~x2    0.007  0.020                                                 
#> y~~y   -0.011 -0.008  0.030                                          
#> x1~~x1  0.022  0.004 -0.004  0.039                                   
#> x1~~x2  0.000 -0.001 -0.001 -0.006  0.005                            
#> x2~~x2 -0.016  0.002  0.011 -0.004 -0.005  0.021                     
#> y~1    -0.006 -0.010  0.007  0.002  0.001 -0.006  0.021              
#> x1~1    0.020  0.000 -0.005  0.009  0.001 -0.010  0.004  0.015       
#> x2~1   -0.026 -0.008 -0.009  0.001  0.000  0.004  0.001 -0.014  0.046
summary(fit)
#> Estimator: MLM
#> Variance method: linearization
#> Design degrees of freedom: 10
#> lavaan 0.7-3 ended normally after 1 iteration
#> 
#>   Estimator                                         ML
#>   Optimization method                           NLMINB
#>   Number of model parameters                         9
#> 
#>   Number of observations                                  48
#>   Sampling weights variable                   .svysem_weight
#> 
#> Model Test User Model:
#>                                               Standard      Scaled
#>   Test Statistic                                 0.000       0.000
#>   Degrees of freedom                                 0           0
#> 
#> Parameter Estimates:
#> 
#>   Standard errors                           Robust.sem
#>   Information                                 Expected
#>   Information saturated (h1) model          Structured
#> 
#> Regressions:
#>                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
#>   y ~                                                 
#>     x1                0.441    0.218    2.020    0.043
#>     x2               -0.483    0.143   -3.384    0.001
#> 
#> Covariances:
#>                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
#>   x1 ~~                                               
#>     x2               -0.085    0.070   -1.210    0.226
#> 
#> Intercepts:
#>                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
#>    .y                 0.902    0.144    6.270    0.000
#>     x1                0.088    0.123    0.715    0.474
#>     x2                0.104    0.214    0.485    0.627
#> 
#> Variances:
#>                    Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
#>    .y                 0.880    0.173    5.076    0.000
#>     x1                0.726    0.197    3.690    0.000
#>     x2                0.958    0.145    6.595    0.000
#> 
cfa_fit <- svycfa("f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4", design)
growth_fit <- svygrowth(
  "i =~ 1*y1 + 1*y2 + 1*y3 + 1*y4
   s =~ 0*y1 + 1*y2 + 2*y3 + 3*y4",
  design
)
coef(cfa_fit)
#>  f=~y2  f=~y3  f=~y4 y1~~y1 y2~~y2 y3~~y3 y4~~y4   f~~f 
#>  1.044  1.071  1.219  0.334  0.118  0.216  0.383  1.053 
coef(growth_fit)
#> y1~~y1 y2~~y2 y3~~y3 y4~~y4   i~~i   s~~s   i~~s    i~1    s~1 
#>  0.266  0.117  0.205  0.295  1.067  0.032  0.031  0.249 -0.039 
predict(cfa_fit)[1, , drop = FALSE]
#>           f
#> 1 0.1295933
mlr_fit <- svycfa("f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4", design, estimator = "MLR")
coef(mlr_fit)
#>  f=~y2  f=~y3  f=~y4 y1~~y1 y2~~y2 y3~~y3 y4~~y4   f~~f 
#>  1.044  1.071  1.219  0.334  0.118  0.216  0.383  1.053
